Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires are back out in the middle and so are the players of Zimbabwe. It will be the pair of former skipper Andy Balbirnie and current skipper Paul Stirling to open the innings for Ireland. Richard Ngarava has the new ball in hand and raring to go. One big blow to the hosts is that Ryan Burl has been ruled out of the game because of a head injury suffered while he was batting.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, the stage is set for the Irish batters to go on and complete the job without a fuss and take a 1-0 lead in the series. Will the home side have an answer with the ball? Let's find out. The run chase is up next.

Zimbabwe and their top-order woes continued as they were overwhelmed by Joshua Little and in all honesty, there were a few poor shots played by the batters as well. Skipper, Sikandar Raza fell with the scorecard reading 19/4 and it looked like all hope was lost for the host. Ryan Burl and Clive Madande stepped up with the latter playing some aggressive cricket and Burl just holding up one end. Madande got into the thirties and got out after whcih Burl stitched together another valiant stand, this time with Wellington Masakadza to put Zimbabwe in a good position but once again it went downhill and they finished well under the 200-run mark. Masakadza was the top scorer and the only one to get into the 40s but it wasn't enough to take his side to a decent total.

A sublime bowling effort from Ireland thanks to a brilliant five-fer from Joshua Little and they have kept the home side, Zimbabwe to an under-apr score of just 166 runs. Little, who was expensive in the last game, made sure to bring his A-game this time and started off in fine fashion, picking up wickets left, right and center. He had the opposition reeling at 19/4, all four wickets to his name and all Ireland needed was to pile on the pressure. However, they faced a bit of resistance but Andy McBrine did get the fifth wicket before Zimbabwe yet again fought back. It was the part-timer, Harry Tector who got the wicket of Ryan Burl and that opened the floodgates. Little came back in and ended up with six wickets to his name and rounded off the best bowling figures in Ireland Men's ODI history.

Commentary.Commentary: Here we go! The umpires and the players are out in the middle to start the second ODI. Tinashe Kamunhukamwe and Joylord Gumbie are the opening batters for Zimbabwe. Mark Adair to start the attack for Ireland. Let's Play!

PITCH REPORT - Darlington Matambanadzo at the pitch report says that the boundaries are big today as it is 75 m behind and 78 m to the squares. The wicket looks really hard on the top and is covered with some live green grass which is definitely going to help the fast bowlers. He adds on by saying that the wicket is much more dry than the first ODI and there is a huge chance that the spinners come into the picture as the match goes on. He ends by saying that it will be a good decision if the captains win the toss and bowl first to make use of the seaming conditions.

The Irish skipper, Paul Stirling says he would have bowled first anyway as the pitch looks the same as the previous match that was washed out. He concludes that the boys can only try to keep the atmosphere light and have fun in the dressing room when the rain stops the action.

Sikandar Raza, the skipper of Zimbabwe states that they will bat first. Adds that it's a dry wicket and they want to put runs on the board. They aim to be a team that doesn't care about the toss and is focused on performing well. Ends by informing that they have a couple of changes in the team with Innocent Kaia missing out due to an injury and Milton Shumba comes in for him. Also, Wellington Masakadza comes in as an extra spinner in place of Luke Jongwe.
Ireland (Unchanged XI) - Paul Stirling (C), Andy Balbirnie, Curtis Campher, Harry Tector, Lorcan Tucker (WK), George Dockrell, Andy McBrine, Mark Adair, Graham Hume, Craig Young, Joshua Little.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Tinashe Kamunhukamwe, Joylord Gumbie (WK), Milton Shumba (In for Innocent Kaia), Sikandar Raza (C), Clive Madande, Ryan Burl, Brandon Mavuta, Tanaka Chivanga, Wellington Masakadza (In for Luke Jongwe), Blessing Muzarabani, Richard Ngarava.
TOSS - Zimbabwe have won the toss and they will BAT first.

Riding high on confidence with the series win in the three-match T20I series, Ireland came into the ODI series well prepared and bowling under overcast conditions, they were right on the money. Mark Adair was brilliant at the top and then the likes of Graham Hume and Craig Young came in and picked up wickets for fun. The only concerning bit for the Irish team is the form of Joshua Little and he has been pretty expensive off late. It will also be interesting to see how their batting fares under similar overcast conditions. Which team will take an unassailable lead in the series? Or will rain play spoilsport yet again? We shall find out. Toss and team news in a bit.

Zimbabwe made as many as seven changes coming into the ODI series as a few of their big-name players like Craig Ervine and Sean Williams were ruled out due to injury. Sikandar Raza led the side in the 1st ODI and while batting first, the inexperience in the lineup showed and they were in trouble at 121/6 before the rain Gods came in and helped them out. They do have a solid bowling lineup but need to tidy things up with the bat in order to get the win against an in-form Ireland side.

Hello and welcome to our coverage of the 2nd ODI between Zimbabwe and Ireland at the Harare Sports Club in Harare. After a fascinating T20I series in which the visitors came back from being 1-0 down to clinch the series 2-1, Ireland were yet again in form in the 1st ODI having Zimbabwe on the ropes but rain played spoilsport and the match was abandoned. As far as this game is concerned, unfortunately, there is still some rain around in Harare but we hope that we are able to get a game in as the forecast is positive ahead.
